newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel barges steady, may rise due to low avails.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel barges steady, may rise due to low avails.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges were steady on Tuesday with some players saying the market stood a good chance of rising further due to better demand and a little supply tightness.

High sulphur barges were done early a little lower than Monday's close, at $82 a tonne fob ARA then moved up to $82.50, $83 a tonne. Some traders said a specific deal for Wednesday delivery was done at $83.50 fob.
"It's on and off activity today. $82, $82.50 and $83 were done (in ARA)," one trader said.

"I believe prices are coming up a little this afternoon... There's demand and there's not much fuel oil available so I think people are willing to pay a little bit more if they want it," the trader added.
Late talk was of $82.50 buying interest and $83.50 selling.

"Most buyers are at $82.50. I think barges will go $1 to $84, $84.50 in the afternoon due to a shortage of avails and some people need the material," a second trader said, adding demand was better than Monday and Friday.
